etymology.text: Traditional 難: phonetic 暵 (abbreviated) + semantic 隹 ‘bird’ — first a kind of bird, borrowed for ‘difficult’; from Proto-Sino-Tibetan *mV-nar ‘to suffer’ (Tibetan མནར mnar).

funFacts: 难 + verb = ‘bad to …’: 难吃, 难喝, 难看, 难听 — and 难过 ‘hard to get through’ = ‘sad’.
我太难了 ‘life is so hard for me’ became one of China’s internet catchphrases in 2019.
pitfalls: 难 nán ‘difficult’ and 难 nàn ‘disaster’ (灾难 zāinàn) are two readings of one character.
‘It’s hard for me’ is 对我来说很难 — *我很难 does not say what you mean.
subtleties: 难 + verb can also be ‘hard to’: 很难说 ‘hard to say’, 很难找 ‘hard to find’.
One syllable: it goes straight before the noun (大房子); with 很 it needs 的 (很大的房子).

Sleepy is 困, not 累: 我困了 ‘I’m sleepy’, 我累了 ‘I’m worn out’.
